hell-on-weils.title: Leptospirosis: reservoir, environment, exposure
hell-on-weils.desc: Reservoir kidney leads to Shed in urine, which leads to Fresh water and wet soil. That water and soil lead back to Reservoir kidney, and also to Broken skin or a mucous membrane. Infected mammals, rats in particular, can carry Leptospira in the kidney and shed it in urine. A person is exposed the same way and is not what keeps the cycle going. Some infections cause no illness. Weil's disease is a severe form.
hell-on-weils.sources: Sources: Levett, Clinical Microbiology Reviews (2001); Haake and Levett, Current Topics in Microbiology and Immunology (2015).

a-sky-full-of-sars--spike.title: SARS coronavirus: spike, receptor and host range
a-sky-full-of-sars--spike.desc: The SARS coronavirus has a crown of spike proteins. A spike binds ACE2, a receptor on a human cell, like a key in a lock. The 2002 to 2003 outbreak in people was followed by the discovery of related coronaviruses in bats, and of a closely related virus in palm civets sold in markets in southern China.
a-sky-full-of-sars--spike.sources: Sources: Li and colleagues, Nature (2003); Li and colleagues, Science (2005); Guan and colleagues, Science (2003).
